title: Cultivation No-Dig
stage: Previously approved photographic set, superseded by revision 09

approval.scope: Page 159 No-Dig proof and all three revision 08 photographs

site: The no-dig bed at the porch end of the back garden. Camera faces the greenhouses. A small strip of grass on the right is an imagined addition requested by John.
timing: Day one: distribute surface compost using a garden fork
One week later: beetroot and spinach plugs in the far half of the same bed; John sets the fifth lettuce at the near end.
wardrobe: Teal fleece, olive beanie and jeans
J01 checked shirt with blue jeans, bareheaded

references_in_order: Storyboard assembled from all three revision-07 PNGs
joint_render.prompt:
Photograph a completely fresh matched THREE-PHOTO SEQUENCE in a single pass for the printed book The Vegetable Guru. Deliver an ultrawide 3:1 contact strip of three independent, equally sized SQUARE colour photographs, edge to edge, hard vertical cuts at exactly 1/3 and 2/3. Maximise native resolution; all three photos fill their square. No text, white rules, margins, title, graphics or numbering. Each square will be cut out and printed on its own, 45 mm wide, above the existing instruction. Re-shoot every frame, including the final planting frame. Reference 1 is the storyboard for composition and succession, reference 2 is the final agreed planting, bed edge, camera position and actor scale to register ALL scenes against; reference 3 is the actual author's face looking down; ref 4 is the documentary photo of his garden in Cornwall; ref 5 identifies the real bareheaded man and checked shirt. The brief is documentary photography of this gardener, not the musician sharing his name.

Same camera on a locked tripod looking away from the porch towards the aluminium greenhouse with brick base; fence with low masonry beneath it, distant black rain barrel, timber berry planter and pots. Porch out of frame. Compose like ref 2 across all three. Our bed is newly made over the near-end lawn, 1.2 metres wide and roughly 4–5 metres long; a rectangular area continuous from broad near end between two pale markers to narrow back end near greenhouse. Narrow little verge of real grass runs on the right. Use identical scale, perspective, camera height, mutually parallel straight sides, corner stones and alignment against wall and greenhouse in all THREE. Registration per square: near-left marker near x=.08 y=.92, near-right at x=.85 y=.95; rear-left corner around x=.70 y=.31, rear-right x=.95 y=.33. Overall straight side lines but individually imperfect edge of freshly spread compost: a few little slumps 2–5 cm over the lawn; uneven crumbs and thin patches catch in grass near the front and along the right edge. Never a pristine laser-cut edge or a bow. Natural dense mown Cornish grass with occasional daisy or plantain leaf. Fresh mulch is dark, friable, slightly fibrous, real colour variation and contact shadows. Keep the teaching action large and hands legible. Same individual, real hands, natural comfortable weight, consistent ordinary human proportions. In ALL frames when John looks down his chin visibly retreats behind his lower lip, beard is short and close to his small recessed chin; jaw sweeps back into collar. Nose, lips then chin step progressively back in side view exactly like ref 3. Do not give him a prominent jaw or pad of beard. Overcast working spring daylight. Same weather and wardrobe during first two shots; a touch brighter but still soft the following week.

LEFT / day 1: John kneeling on grass LEFT of bed, olive knitted beanie, teal fleece over dark jumper, worn jeans and boots. Plain flattened, damp brown corrugated cartons generously OVERLAP directly on intact lawn. Use varied realistic reused cartons with fold lines, tape and staples removed, as real ref 4. John's hands are just lowering the near sheet over the previous one, one seam clearly visible, no weeds or lawn in the joins. Full cardboard bed outline, already mostly covered up to far end. No compost, tools etc in this first frame. Natural incidental pose.

MIDDLE / same day: John now stands on the left lawn, same clothes and hat, in the same patch of ground. John is caught spreading a loose small forkful of mature compost horizontally over the card surface; the earth is NOT dug or turned. Show an actual ordinary, well-proportioned British digging fork: D-handle, wooden shaft to a centred socket and one narrow forged head with FOUR sturdy, spaced, slightly curved prongs projecting down the continuation of the shaft. No transverse rake head. One hand on D-handle and the other down shaft, four tines just over the compost deliberately rolling off a last clump. Surface level is about 10 cm of compost across most of bed. A small amount of cardboard still visible at unfinished far end, a couple of low mounds and crumbs spilling onto margin. No plants growing in this bed yet.

RIGHT / one week later: recreate the scene in ref 2: same greenhouse, two stones and broad straight bed, now planted as mixed no-dig bed. Bareheaded John, his real receding hairline, cream/charcoal/plum checked overshirt sleeves rolled over dark T-shirt, blue jeans. Relaxed on his knees on left grass; face turned to the right in near-profile looking at his hands, recognisably recessed small chin. In the FAR HALF of the same bed there are a few short rows of young spinach with dark matt green leaves at the very back then young beetroot with slender red stems and veins. Red and green groups visibly distinct, open compost between young transplants, no full-sized crops. Leave the middle foreground largely bare. At the NEAR end EXACTLY FIVE little lettuce plugs across ONE transverse row in total. One is at John's fingertips at the left, FOUR separately countable ones to its right. Across the full 1.2 m bed, regularly about 24 cm apart (10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90% across the bed at planting depth); damp small leaves with restrained natural mid-green, 3–5 true leaves as in the accepted reference. Discrete contact shadows, crowns partly upright with a few naturally curled leaves. A modest black module tray by John's knee on the left grass with a few spare matching lettuce seedlings and vacant cells. No extras in the bed. Give the compost edge the small natural spills here too. Ref 2 is authoritative for crop count and straight footprint. Keep real-world scale and the quiet photojournalistic look across all three frames, clear visual sequence, no studio polish.
